result.title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
result.summary: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under matched budgets. Prior work demonstrates that different loop visits can play different roles even when they share parameters. To probe the contributions of different loop visits, we learn separate residual coefficients in a model that applies a shared block twice, observing a smaller scale in the first visit. Fixed coefficient experiments show that reducing the first visit's scale preserves or improves performance, whereas the same reductions to the second hurt it. This asymmetry motivates us to explore asymmetric compute allocation. We propose \textbf{LatentLoop}, which compresses the first visit's sequence, retains full resolution in the second, and reallocates saved computation to increase the hidden size. We further learn how strongly the first visit updates the full sequence, and share MoE weights across visits while using separate attention parameters to accommodate their different sequence resolutions. Across 15 configurations spanning 1.3B--7B parameters, with the largest budget exceeding $10^{21}$ FLOPs, LatentLoop consistently lowers validation NLL. At a fitted NLL of 1.988, predicted compute savings are 19.0\% and 7.9\% relative to vanilla MoE and the looped baseline. It also improves average scores on nine benchmarks at all sizes in 0-shot and 5-shot settings. These results suggest asymmetric compute allocation is a promising direction for looped MoE models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 looped MoE 中不同循环访问的角色差异：首轮访问的残差尺度更小且压缩它不损性能，据此提出 LatentLoop——压缩第一轮序列、第二轮保留全分辨率，节省的算力用于扩大隐藏维度，在 1.3B–7B 多配置下降低验证 NLL 并提升九个基准成绩。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同一权重下不同循环访问贡献不对称」的观察、首轮序列压缩与可学习的首轮更新强度系数，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理步骤的算力分配、状态压缩与细节保留之间的权衡提供可供核查的方法线索，但原文为纯语言建模设定，需人工判断迁移可行性。
